ActivitySummary.description:
`details` is a JSON string, not a nested object: Groq's strict
schema mode requires every object field to list fixed `properties`
(verified against console.groq.com/docs/structured-outputs,
2026-09-03) -- it does not support an open, arbitrary-key dict like
activities.details actually is (irrigation vs fertiliser vs spray
each have different fields). This field is read-only evidence shown
to the model, never written back, so a JSON string is sufficient and
keeps the schema valid without inventing a fixed shape that doesn't
exist yet.
ActivitySummary.title: ActivitySummary

AdvisoryRecord.description:
A saved answer. `response` is the AdvisoryResponse exactly as it was when
the farmer received it, kept as a plain object on purpose: that contract
grows, and an old row must never fail to load because of a newer schema.
AdvisoryRecord.title: AdvisoryRecord

EvidenceItem.description:
One retrieved passage that a VALIDATED citation points at. Every field
except `quote` is copied by code from the chunk/document row.
EvidenceItem.title: EvidenceItem

FarmUpdate.description:
PATCH body: only the fields sent are changed (`exclude_unset`), and an
explicit null clears a nullable field. Needed because a farm created
without a location or soil type could otherwise never gain one, and the
irrigation water balance (ADR-0015) needs both.
FarmUpdate.title: FarmUpdate

LabelEntry.description:
One label card in the farmer's response. Every field is copied by code
from a verified table row; the model never authors any of it.
LabelEntry.title: LabelEntry

ModelSaw.description:
What the second (vision-language) model reported about the photo, forced into a closed vocabulary.
`symptoms` is its one free sentence, after the dose and banned-molecule guards.
ModelSaw.title: ModelSaw

ScanFeedback.description:
The farmer's own verdict on a photo check. `confirmed_label` is a class of the label map (checked in
the router) when the farmer says the real problem was a different one.
ScanFeedback.title: ScanFeedback

ScanRecord.description:
A saved photo check. `response` is the DiagnosisResponse exactly as the farmer received it, kept
as a plain object on purpose: that contract grows, and an old row must never fail to load.
ScanRecord.title: ScanRecord

WaterBalanceResult.description:
What the farmer's response carries as `water_balance`: computed by
code, never written by the model.
WaterBalanceResult.title: WaterBalanceResult

get.description:
Readiness check — proves the app can actually reach Postgres and
read real data (the crops seeded by migration 0004).

delete.description:
The farmer removes a photo check and its photo. Row first (so nothing points at a deleted photo),
then the object; a failure to delete the object is logged, not shown: the row is already gone.

get.description:
Proves the full chain: JWT verified -> role/claims set in Postgres
-> auth.uid() resolves inside the database. jwt_sub and db_auth_uid
must be equal and non-null for RLS to work at all.
